@metadata.comment: The website's own pages (Milestone 24): Why Plot Device, Support, In your language. The guide's pages are translated as pages, in src/content/docs.

home-title: Plot Device: a calm writing studio for novelists
home-description: Write first, see the story, and keep your book as a folder of plain Markdown files. In Hebrew and English.
hero-title: Write the novel. Keep the files.
hero-lede: A calm desk for your chapters, a clear view of your story, and a folder of plain Markdown files that stays yours.
platforms: Early versions for Linux and Windows · macOS later
hero-shot-alt: Plot Device's writing desk: the chapter list, and a chapter of The Salt Orchard on the page
write-text: No outline to fill in, no setup. The page waits under a soft light; formatting appears only when you select text, and the rest of the app stays out of your way.
write-alt: Selected text in a chapter, with a small formatting bubble above it
story-title: The shape of the book, at a glance.
story-text: Plan in outlines that are simply Markdown lists: on a board, as a list, or as text. Drag a card, link it to a chapter or a character, and your prose stays exactly as you wrote it.
story-alt: An outline on a board: Beginning, Middle and End, with cards linked to chapters and characters
timeline-title: Who was where, while it happened.
timeline-text: Give each storyline an outline of its own, and see them all side by side on the timeline. Drag a moment onto another to say they happen at the same time; everything else falls into place. It's still your outlines, in your files: nothing is drawn by hand.
timeline-alt: The timeline: the main story on top, with Bea's path and Ilka's arc lined up under its moments
references-text: Characters, places and notes, or whatever your book needs, such as factions or ships, sit beside the page while you write. Search, pin the ones you need, and never lose your place in the chapter.
references-alt: A chapter with the references shelf open, showing Bea Halmi's page pinned
bilingual-title: The interface in your language. The book in its own.
bilingual-text: Write a Hebrew novel with English names, or an English one in a Hebrew interface. Every paragraph runs the right way, and punctuation lands where it belongs.
bilingual-alt: A Hebrew chapter, right to left, in Plot Device's English interface
files-title: A folder of plain Markdown. Yours, for good.
files-text: Every chapter is a Markdown file, the book's order is a readable list, and outlines are ordinary lists. Open the same folder in Obsidian, any text editor or git: Plot Device is a lens on your files, not a place that locks them in.
yours-title: No account. No cloud. No claim on your work.
yours-text: Plot Device runs on your computer and sends nothing anywhere. If you want, it keeps a backup of the book each day, in a folder you choose. What you write belongs to you, under your own copyright.
closing-support: Plot Device is made by one person. If it helps your writing, $1.
support-description: Who makes Plot Device, what your support makes possible, and the ways to help.
support-lede: Plot Device is made by one person, for writers who would rather write than wrestle with software.
support-cost: Plot Device is free to use. It isn't free to make: every feature, fix and translation takes time. If it helps your writing, your support is truly appreciated.
support-makes-time: More time for Plot Device: fixes, and the things writers ask for.
support-makes-languages: More languages, for the app and its guide.
support-makes-calm: Keeping it calm: no ads, no account, and nothing sent from your computer.
support-coffee-text: Any amount, once or every month. It goes straight into making Plot Device.
support-coffee-button: Support on Buy Me a Coffee
support-tell-text: Most writers find their tools through a friend. A word in your writing group helps more than you would think.
support-report-text: If something doesn't work the way you expect, say so. Every report makes Plot Device better for the next writer.
support-translate-text: Ask for your language, or help translate Plot Device for writers who speak it.
support-no-pressure: None of this is expected. If you just want to write, that's what Plot Device is for.
languages-description: The languages Plot Device speaks, how to ask for yours, and how to help translate it.
languages-lede: Plot Device speaks English and Hebrew today, right to left included. It's built to take more: each new language is a translation, not a rewrite.
languages-today-text: The app, its guide and this site are in:
languages-today-book: The book and the interface can be in different languages: write a Hebrew novel in an English interface, or the other way round.
languages-ask-text: Say which language you'd like to use Plot Device in. Knowing where writers are waiting helps decide which language comes next.
languages-form-email-hint: Only to tell you when your language arrives. Nothing else.
languages-translate-text: Know English or Hebrew, and another language well? Translating Plot Device is mostly writing. The guide explains how.
thanks-description: Your request for a language was sent.
thanks-text: Your request is in. If you left an email address, you'll hear when your language arrives.
home-compare: How Plot Device compares with other writing apps
compare-description: Plot Device beside Google Docs, Word, Scrivener, Dabble, Novelcrafter, Campfire and Obsidian: languages, where your writing is kept, AI, and tools for novels.
compare-checked: Checked on $1, from each company's own pages. Things change; if something here is out of date, $2.
compare-not-documented-note: "Not documented" means the company's own pages don't say, so the table doesn't guess.
compare-table-caption: Plot Device and seven other writing apps, compared
compare-row-files: Your book opens in other apps
compare-row-export: Saves as Word, PDF and EPUB
compare-cell-computers-gdocs: Web browser, phone and tablet apps
compare-cell-computers-word: Windows, Mac, phones and tablets, web
compare-cell-computers-dabble: Web, and as an app on most systems
compare-cell-computers-obsidian: Windows, Mac, Linux, phones and tablets
compare-cell-ui-pd: English and Hebrew; built for more
compare-cell-ai-word: Copilot built in; can be turned off
compare-cell-ai-obsidian: Yes; plugins by others add it
compare-cell-files-scrivener: Its own format; exports to others
compare-cell-planning-pd: Outline board, timeline, characters and places
compare-different-stays: Plot Device works on your computer. It needs no account and no internet, and it never sends your book to another service, so no company can read it, keep it or use it to train AI. Online writing apps keep your book on their servers, under their terms.
compare-different-ai: Plot Device has no AI of its own. What you write is read by you, and by whoever you choose to share it with.
compare-different-files: Your book is a folder of ordinary text files, not a format only Plot Device can open. Open it in another app today, or in twenty years.
compare-different-backups: Backups are plain copies of your book in a folder you choose, on your computer or a drive you already sync. Plot Device never uploads them, and they open without it.
compare-different-languages: The menus come in English and Hebrew, and each new language is a translation away. Right-to-left writing, in Hebrew, Arabic or Persian, works paragraph by paragraph, even with English in the middle of a sentence.
compare-different-novels: Outlines on a board, a timeline of every storyline, and pages for your characters and places, beside the page while you write.
compare-sources-text: Each answer comes from the company's own pages, checked on the date above.
compare-hero-title: Your book. Your computer. Your language.
compare-hero-lede: Plot Device is a calm writing studio for novels that keeps everything with you: no account, no AI, no one else's servers. Here is how it stands beside the tools writers use most.
compare-closing-title: Use it with your existing book.
compare-closing-text: Import a Word file, or start a new book. Your files are always yours.
compare-move-title: Work on the book you already have
compare-move-text: Already writing in Word or Google Docs? Import your manuscript as a Word file, and Plot Device splits it into chapters, showing you how before anything is made. Your Word file is never changed.
compare-move-link: How importing a Word file works
download-description: Download Plot Device for Windows or Linux. A Mac version is on its way.
download-lede: Version $1, released $2. No account and no sign-up: download it, open it, and write.
download-none: The downloads will be here soon. Until then, Plot Device's files are on GitHub.
download-on-phone: Plot Device is an app for computers. Open this page on your computer to download it.
download-windows-note: An early version. Windows may say it doesn't recognise the app: choose More info, then Run anyway.
download-appimage-note: Works on any Linux. Allow it to run once after downloading.
download-deb-note: For Ubuntu and Debian. Installs with your other apps.
download-mac-note: A Mac version is on its way. It needs an Apple developer account first, so $1 helps it arrive sooner.
download-after-text: The guide shows how to open Plot Device the first time and start your book, step by step.
download-after-link: How to install and open it
download-previous-text: In case you need an older version. The newest is usually the best choice.
download-support: Plot Device is made by one person. If it helps your writing, $1 is truly appreciated.
